svg.text: Figure 8 - Filing transactions without a CAM
Because address bits pick the bank directly, we can file each request into the right list on arrival. Row-hit batching then falls out for free.
{ valid, wr, bg, ba, row, col,
if (row == grp_row[bank][dir]) append to the current tail group
Same-row requests end up physically CONTIGUOUS in the list, so when the
head is reached they issue as a burst of row hits. No content-addressable
head_is_row_hit[b] = (grp_row at head == open row of bank b)
Maintained incrementally as a 32-bit vector, so the arbiter
sees a mask, not a comparison tree.
The limit you should know about
Strict per-bank FIFO order means a row hit sitting behind a row miss TO THE SAME BANK has to wait.
Under the STREAM address map this essentially never happens, because consecutive accesses to one
pseudo-channel go to DIFFERENT banks. For random traffic, set GROUP_HOIST_EN to let a newer same-row
group jump ahead - bounded by HOIST_MAX = 8 so the starvation guarantee survives.
